messages:
Maya L: Heads up — our scanner bumped an OpenSSL 3.x vuln for alpine-slim images used in inference runtime.
Jordan P: specific CVE?
Maya L: CVE-2026-XXXX, shows up in SBOM for image: redwood/inference-runtime:alpine-slim-20260209
Samir: Is this in prod? where did scanner find it?
Maya L: Found in nightly image build uploaded to registry. No serve nodes running that tag in prod yet. Canary staging pool has an older tag but I'll check.
Irene K: TL;DR: prioritize rebuild + sign -> push -> canary -> promote. Need RBAC for who can sign images and which KMS key to use.
sec-bot: [automated] vulnerability severity: HIGH, CVSS 8.2. Suggested action: rebuild + update OpenSSL or switch base image.
Jordan P: We should avoid last-minute glibc swaps. For alpine, bump openssl package to 3.1.6 and rebuild. Also regen SBOM.
Samir: Agreed. Proposed priority matrix: 1) High exploitability + public exposure -> rebuild now; 2) High but no prod exposure -> schedule within 48h; 3) Medium/Low -> batch next weekly run.
Irene K: Who owns signing? Current CI uses `ci-bot` to sign artifacts with KMS alias `alias/redwood-image-signer` in AWS. Need to restrict to `infra-image-signers` group and require MFA for manual overrides.
Oliver D: I'll add an RBAC rule: `iam:PassRole` only for `infra-image-signers` and a Terraform change to lock the KMS key policy. Also add audit log filter for kms:Sign in CloudTrail.
DevOps: CI change: new job `image:rebuild-and-sign` will run after successful package updates. Snippet:
```
jobs:
  rebuild-and-sign:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - run: docker build --pull --no-cache -t $REGISTRY/$IMAGE:$NEW_TAG .
      - run: docker push $REGISTRY/$IMAGE:$NEW_TAG
      - run: |
          aws kms sign --key-id alias/redwood-image-signer \
            --message fileb://manifest.json --output json > sig.json
```
Maya L: Two operational checks before promoting: 1) SBOM diff shows only patched openssl and deps, 2) quick e2e on canary staging (10% traffic) for 4 hours.
Samir: Add rollout policy in Console: automatic rollback on any crashrate > 0.5% or latency regression >10%.
Irene K: Also add ephemeral signing keys for CI agents rotated daily; use KMS Envelope encryption and store audit entries in LogRetention bucket.
Jordan P: Timeline? Can we have a canary build by EOD?
DevOps: I'll queue the rebuild and attach labels: `security:patched-cve-2026-XXXX`. Expect canary image by 1834568000 (ETA ~2m).
sec-bot: [automated] created issue #SEC-812 in security backlog.
Maya L: Thanks — once canary passes, we'll schedule production promotion during next release window (tomorrow 10:00 UTC) unless any concerns.
Oliver D: I'll open a PR for the KMS policy and RBAC group; pinging @Irene K for review :eyes:
Irene K: reviewing now. If no blockers, I'll approve and merge.
Jordan P: add note to run full dependency scan after merge and notify customers on affected images in case they pinned exact tags. :warning:
Maya L: good call. I'll draft a short advisory in #announcements if prod is impacted.
ci-bot: build 1243 started for redwood/inference-runtime:alpine-slim-20260209-patch
DevOps: build succeeded, pushed tag, signing step completed :shipit:
Maya L: canary started. Monitoring dashboards linked: https://console.redwood.internal/dashboards/canary/1834567890
Samir: :thumbsup: good job team, keep an eye on audit logs for any anomalous signing attempts.
